example_narratives.narrative: Driver took over on a straight urban road under low-sun conditions with clear lane markings and no detected lead object. The gentle 1 mph speed drop and minimal brake pressure (0 bar) with low steering torque (3.7 Nm) indicate a voluntary takeover rather than a safety intervention.

Lane-detection confidence dropped from 0.82 to 0.49 due to orange traffic cones lining the left side of the road in a construction zone, causing the system to hand over to the driver. The driver took control with minimal deceleration (0.4 m/s²) and moderate steering inputs, indicating the system's degraded performance in the work zone rather than an imminent collision risk.

Heavy snowfall obscured lane markings and reduced camera visibility to 0.62, causing lane-detection confidence to drop to 0.38, which triggered a system deactivation. The vehicle maintained constant speed with minimal braking and steering input, indicating the system handed over due to degraded perception rather than an immediate collision threat.

The vehicle initiated hard braking (5.1 m/s² deceleration, 27 mph speed drop) on a rainy highway under an overpass with no lead object detected. The perception system likely generated a false positive detection, possibly from reflection or sensor artifacts in the rain beneath the bridge structure, triggering an unnecessary safety intervention.

Heavy snow at night reduced camera visibility to 0.12 and caused lane-detection confidence to drop to 0.33, exceeding the system's perceptual limits for 10 seconds. The system deactivated appropriately as environmental conditions prevented safe autonomous operation without driver intervention.

The system deactivated on a clear highway during low-sun conditions (golden hour). Camera visibility dropped to 0.44 for 0.2 seconds due to sun glare, causing a transient perception degradation that triggered the handover despite a lead vehicle being visible in the scene.
